reason: The text demonstrates multiple instances of people freely expressing their views and concerns. A woman openly cries out to the king for help (וַאִשָּׁה צָעֲקָה אֵלָיו), and the king responds receptively to her complaint, asking for explanation. The lepers discuss their situation openly (אִישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵהוּ), deliberate about their options, and freely communicate their findings to the gatekeepers. The king consults with his servants (וַיֹּאמֶר אֶל־ עֲבָדָיו), and a servant boldly offers strategic advice (וַיַּעַן אֶחָד מֵעֲבָדָיו). Throughout the passage, people at all social levels—women, lepers, common servants, and advisors—express their views without apparent restriction. The text shows no discouragement of speech or suppression of views; rather, it depicts open communication across social hierarchies.
